toc.title: Configuring remote state with the backend block

html:
1What a backend is

A backend defines where Terraform stores its state and how operations run.

Backend Where state lives
local (the default) A file terraform.tfstate in the working directory (path can be changed)
Remote (for example S3, Azure Blob Storage, Google Cloud Storage, Consul, a database) Shared storage outside your machine
HCP Terraform (the cloud block) HCP Terraform workspaces (Module 16)

2The local backend

Fact Detail
Default Used when no backend is configured
File terraform.tfstate, and terraform.tfstate.backup for the previous version
Locking Locks the file while an operation runs (system file locking)
Limits Not shared; no encryption or versioning; unsuitable for teams
Configure path backend "local" { path = "..." }
Exam tip

. The local backend is the default and stores terraform.tfstate next to your configuration. It is fine for learning and bad for teams.

3Configuring remote state with the backend block

The backend block is nested in the terraform block. A configuration has at most one backend.

terraform {
  backend "s3" {
    bucket       = "example-terraform-state"
    key          = "network/terraform.tfstate"
    region       = "us-east-1"
    encrypt      = true
    use_lockfile = true
  }
}
Rule Detail
No variables or references Backend arguments must be literal values; use partial configuration (terraform init -backend-config=...) or environment variables for the rest
Credentials Supply them outside the file (environment variables, instance roles)
After adding or changing a backend Run terraform init; Terraform offers to migrate the state (-migrate-state); -reconfigure ignores the old settings
Benefits Sharing, locking, encryption, versioning, access control

Reading another configuration's state: the terraform_remote_state data source reads the root-module outputs of another state.

data "terraform_remote_state" "network" {
  backend = "s3"
  config = {
    bucket = "example-terraform-state"
    key    = "network/terraform.tfstate"
    region = "us-east-1"
  }
}
Exam tip

. Backend settings cannot use variables. terraform_remote_state exposes only the root outputs of the other configuration.

4State locking

State locking prevents two operations from writing the state at the same time, which could corrupt it.

Fact Detail
When it locks During operations that could write state: plan, apply, destroy and some state commands
Automatic On by default where the backend supports it
Backend support Most remote backends (for example S3 with a lock file, Azure, Google Cloud Storage); not every backend
-lock=false Turns locking off (dangerous)
-lock-timeout=DURATION Wait for a lock to be released instead of failing at once
terraform force-unlock LOCK_ID Releases a stuck lock (use only if no run is active)
Exam tip

. Locking prevents concurrent state changes. force-unlock is for a stuck lock only, and -lock=false is rarely a good idea.

5Exam Q&A

5.1 Practice questions (choose the best answer)

S1A configuration has no backend block. Where is the state stored?

  • AIn HCP Terraform
  • BIn a file named terraform.tfstate in the working directory
  • CIn the provider's cloud console
  • DIn the module registry
Show the answer

Answer: B. Without a backend block the local backend stores terraform.tfstate in the working directory.

S2A team wants shared, encrypted, locked state. What should they configure?

  • AA local backend with a much larger shared disk
  • BA remote backend in the terraform block
  • CA provider alias for each person
  • DA data block for the state
Show the answer

Answer: B. A remote backend stores state in shared storage and supports locking.

S3Can the arguments of a backend block use input variables?

  • AYes, through var references
  • BNo, they must be literal values or supplied another way
  • CYes, through local values
  • DYes, through data sources
Show the answer

Answer: B. Backend settings cannot use variables or references; use partial configuration or environment variables.

S4What is the purpose of state locking?

  • ATo hide secrets in the state
  • BTo speed up the plan
  • CTo encrypt the state in transit
  • DTo prevent concurrent operations from corrupting the state
Show the answer

Answer: D. Locking stops two operations from writing the state at the same time.

S5A run crashed and left a lock behind. No one else is running Terraform. What can be used?

  • Aterraform init -upgrade
  • Bterraform force-unlock with the lock ID
  • Cterraform fmt -lock
  • Dterraform validate -unlock
Show the answer

Answer: B. force-unlock releases a stuck lock, and should only be used when no run is active.

S6What does the terraform_remote_state data source provide?

  • AThe provider versions of another configuration
  • BThe resource attributes of every resource in another state
  • CThe variables of another configuration
  • DThe root module outputs of another configuration's state
Show the answer

Answer: D. It reads the root-module outputs stored in another state.

5.2 Recall questions

R1What is the default backend?

Show the answer

The local backend.

R2Where is the backend block written?

Show the answer

Inside the terraform block.

R3Can backend arguments use variables?

Show the answer

No.

R4What does state locking prevent?

Show the answer

Concurrent changes that corrupt the state.

R5Which command releases a stuck lock?

Show the answer

terraform force-unlock.

R6What happens after changing the backend?

Show the answer

Run terraform init; Terraform can migrate the state.

6Quick Reference Card

Topic Key fact
Backends local (default, terraform.tfstate), remote (S3, Azure, GCS, Consul), HCP Terraform (cloud block)
Backend block in the terraform block; one only; literal values; init after changes
Remote state sharing, locking, encryption, versioning; terraform_remote_state reads outputs
Locking automatic where supported; -lock=false, -lock-timeout, force-unlock
